b_srikakulam.etymology_analysis: Telugu/Sanskrit Srikakulam (known as Chicacole in colonial records), associated with the Srikakuleswara shrine and later regional administration under the Golconda Qutb Shahis.

b_swetakapura.first_mention_attestation: Attested as 'Shvetaka' (Swetakapura, modern Chikiti in Ganjam district, Odisha), capital of the collateral Shvetaka branch of the Eastern Gangas, in 7th–8th-century CE copperplate charters including Samantavarman's Pherava grant and Jayavarmadeva's Ganjam grant (c. 756–786 CE, under Bhauma-Kara overlord Shivakara I).
b_swetakapura.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit 'Shvetakapura' ('City of Shvetaka', derived from 'shveta' 'white' + '-ka' + 'pura' 'city'), capital of the collateral Shvetaka branch of the Eastern Gangas at modern Chikiti in Ganjam district, Odisha, attested in 7th–9th century CE copperplate charters.

b_rayagada.first_mention_attestation: 1527–1531 CE (founded by King Vishwanath Dev Gajapati of the Suryavamsa dynasty of Nandapur)
b_rayagada.etymology_analysis: Odia Rayagada ('royal fort'), founded in the early 16th century CE (1527–1531 CE) by Vishwanath Dev Gajapati of Nandapur.

b_asurgarh.first_mention_attestation: Modern Odia name of an Iron Age / early historic fortified site (5th century BCE–5th century CE) with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation of the name Asurgarh
b_asurgarh.etymology_analysis: Odia Asurgarh ('fort of the Asuras', or locally derived from Asokagarh), a modern designation for the early historic fortified settlement in Kalahandi district, Odisha.

b_vizagipatam.first_mention_attestation: 1068 CE (Inscription No. 187 of 1893, recording Visakhapatnam under King Visakhavarma)
b_vizagipatam.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit/Telugu Visakhapatnam ('city of Visakha', anglicized as Vizagapatam), first documented in a 1068 CE inscription.

b_nandapur.first_mention_attestation: Medieval capital of the Silavamsa dynasty in the 14th century CE, with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation
b_nandapur.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit/Odia Nandapur ('city of Nanda / joy'), a historic seat in Koraput district, Odisha, attested as the capital of the 14th-century CE Silavamsa rulers.

b_katak.first_mention_attestation: c. 913 CE (three copper-plate grants issued from Kataka in the 31st regnal year of Somavamshi king Janmejaya I, r. c. 882–922 CE)
b_katak.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Kataka ('royal camp, cantonment, fort'), modern Cuttack, first attested in early 10th-century CE Somavamshi grants and later made the Eastern Ganga capital c. 1135 CE.

b_bhubaneswar.first_mention_attestation: 1058 CE (Brahmeswara Temple inscription of Kolavati Devi, 18th regnal year of Somavamshi king Uddyotakeshari, referring to the Shaivite center)
b_bhubaneswar.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Tribhuvanesvara / Bhuvanesvara ('Lord of the Three Worlds', an epithet of Shiva), superseding the earlier name Ekamra / Ekambaka.

historical_names.name: Ekambaka
historical_names.source: Vigraha dynasty copper-plate inscription dated Gupta year 280 (600 CE)
historical_names.notes: Before adopting the name Bhubaneswar (from Tribhuvanesvara), the Old Town temple complex was attested as Ekambaka / Ekamra in a 600 CE Vigraha inscription.

historical_names.name: Ekamra
historical_names.source: Vigraha dynasty copper-plate inscription dated Gupta year 280 (600 CE)
historical_names.notes: Before adopting the name Bhubaneswar (from Tribhuvanesvara), the Old Town temple complex was attested as Ekambaka / Ekamra in a 600 CE Vigraha inscription.

b_konarak.first_mention_attestation: c. 1250 CE (construction of the Konark Sun Temple under Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I)
b_konarak.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Konarka ('corner sun'), referring to the Sun Temple of Surya built c. 1250 CE by Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I.

b_dhauli.first_mention_attestation: Modern Odia hill/village name with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation (site of Ashoka's c. 256 BCE Rock Edicts naming Tosali)
b_dhauli.etymology_analysis: Modern Odia toponym Dhauli (from Dhavali, 'white hill'), located near ancient Tosali where Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts were inscribed.

historical_names.name: Tosali
historical_names.source: Separate Kalinga Edicts of Ashoka at Dhauli (c. 256 BCE)
historical_names.notes: Ashoka's Dhauli Rock Edicts name the Mauryan administrative center Tosali (associated with the Dhauli-Sisupalgarh complex).

b_sakshigopal.first_mention_attestation: Late medieval / modern pilgrimage town name (associated with Gajapati Purushottama Deva, late 15th century CE) with no datable pre-867 CE attestation
b_sakshigopal.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit/Odia Sakshigopala ('witness Gopal', i.e., Krishna as witness), the deity of the Sakhigopal Temple in Puri district, Odisha (formerly called Satyabadi).

b_athgarh.first_mention_attestation: 1178 CE (foundation of Athgarh State by Raja Srikaran Niladri Bebarta Patnaik)
b_athgarh.etymology_analysis: Odia Athagada / Athgarh ('eight forts'), the capital of the former Athgarh princely state founded in 1178 CE.

b_khijjinga.first_mention_attestation: 924 CE (Bamanghaty copper-plate inscription of Adi-Bhanja ruler Ranabhanja, dated year 188)
b_khijjinga.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Khijjingakota ('fort of Khijjinga', modern Khiching in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha), capital of the Adi-Bhanja dynasty, first firmly dated in the 924 CE Bamanghaty charter.

b_asanapat.first_mention_attestation: Modern village name in Keonjhar district, Odisha (site of the 4th-century CE Nataraja stone inscription of Naga ruler Satrubhanja, published in 1965 CE) with no datable pre-867 CE attestation of the village name itself
b_asanapat.etymology_analysis: Modern Odia village name Asanapat in Keonjhar district, Odisha, where the 4th-century CE Sanskrit stone inscription of Naga king Satrubhanja was discovered.

b_bahalda.first_mention_attestation: Medieval Mayurbhanj capital in the 13th–14th centuries CE with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation
b_bahalda.etymology_analysis: Regional Odia/Munda toponym Bahalda in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, which served as a capital of the Mayurbhanj Bhanjas in the 13th–14th centuries CE.

b_ghatagaon.first_mention_attestation: Late medieval / modern town name in Keonjhar district, Odisha (associated with the Maa Tarini shrine, traditionally dated 15th–17th century CE) with no datable pre-867 CE attestation
b_ghatagaon.etymology_analysis: Odia Ghatagaon ('village at the pass/ghat'), located in Kendujhar district, Odisha, famed for the Maa Tarini temple.

b_malayagiri.first_mention_attestation: Modern/traditional mountain peak name in Angul district, Odisha, with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation
b_malayagiri.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit/Odia Malayagiri ('Malaya mountain'), directly adopting the proper name of the prominent peak in the Garhjat Range of Angul district, Odisha.

b_khinjali.first_mention_attestation: Mid-8th century CE (c. 750–800 CE; Sonepur copper-plate grant of Bhanja king Satrubhanja I, son of Silabhanja I)
b_khinjali.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Khinjali-Mandala ('province of Khinjali'), the early medieval principality of the Bhanja dynasty centered in the Boudh-Phulbani-Sonepur region, attested in 8th-century CE copper plates.

b_nilamadhav.first_mention_attestation: Temple/shrine name at Kantilo, Nayagarh district, Odisha, with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation
b_nilamadhav.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit/Odia Nilamadhava ('blue Madhava'), a manifestation of Vishnu worshipped at the Nilamadhav Temple in Kantilo on the Mahanadi River.

b_nayagarh.first_mention_attestation: c. 1480–1510 CE (reputed foundation of Baghua Nayagarh by local chieftain Baghel Singh)
b_nayagarh.etymology_analysis: Odia/Indo-Aryan Nayagarh ('new fort'), the capital of the former Nayagarh State founded in the late 15th century CE.

b_viraja.first_mention_attestation: 865 CE (Dhauli cave inscription of Bhauma-Kara king Santikaradeva, year 93, naming Bhatta Loyomaka of Viraja, alongside Bhauma-Kara copper plates)
b_viraja.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Viraja ('pure, free from passion', and name of the presiding goddess Viraja/Biraja), the ancient name of Jajpur in Odisha, attested in Bhauma-Kara epigraphs by 865 CE.

b_ratnagiri.first_mention_attestation: 8th–9th century CE (monastic clay seals and stone/terracotta inscriptions from the Ratnagiri Mahavihara in Jajpur district, Odisha)
b_ratnagiri.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Ratnagiri ('hill of jewels'), the major Buddhist monastic complex (mahavihara) in Odisha's Diamond Triangle active from the 5th–6th centuries CE and epigraphically attested in 8th–9th century CE seals and inscriptions.

b_bhadrak.first_mention_attestation: Modern/medieval town name derived from Goddess Bhadrakali with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation (the 3rd-century CE Bhadrak inscription of Gana records Panida)
b_bhadrak.etymology_analysis: Odia toponym Bhadrak, derived from the presiding deity Bhadrakali (whose shrine lies near the town).

historical_names.name: Panida
historical_names.source: Bhadrak stone inscription of Mahārāja Gaṇa (c. 3rd century CE)
historical_names.notes: The 3rd-century CE Bhadrak inscription of Gaṇa records the locality/administrative unit Panida prior to the medieval/modern name Bhadrak.

b_baleshvara.first_mention_attestation: Post-medieval coastal town name (anglicized Balasore; English factory established 1634 CE) with no datable pre-867 CE attestation
b_baleshvara.etymology_analysis: Odia Baleswara / Baleshvara (anglicized Balasore), regionally derived from Baneswara (Shiva), the presiding deity of Puruna Baleswar.

b_raibania.first_mention_attestation: 13th century CE (c. 1238–1264 CE; fort complex built during the reign of Eastern Ganga ruler Narasimhadeva I, later recorded in the Ain-i-Akbari)
b_raibania.etymology_analysis: Odia Raibania, the medieval fort complex in Balasore district built under Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I (13th century CE).

b_kodalaka.first_mention_attestation: c. 839 CE (copper-plate inscriptions of Sulki ruler Ranastambha and the Sulki dynasty of Kodalaka Mandala)
b_kodalaka.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Kodalaka-Mandala ('province of Kodalaka', modern Kualo in Dhenkanal district, Odisha), the 9th-century CE principality of the Sulki feudatories under the Bhauma-Karas.

b_bajrakot.first_mention_attestation: Modern/medieval village name in Angul district, Odisha, with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation
b_bajrakot.etymology_analysis: Odia/Sanskrit Bajrakot ('thunderbolt fort'), a village in Angul district, Odisha, known for the medieval Bhringesvara Shiva temple.

b_deogarh.first_mention_attestation: Modern/early modern town name (Debagarh, former capital of Bamra State) with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation
b_deogarh.etymology_analysis: Odia/Indo-Aryan Deogarh / Debagarh ('fort of the gods'), the former capital of the Bamanda (Bamra) princely state in northwestern Odisha.

b_puri.first_mention_attestation: Late 11th century CE (c. 1078 CE; Prabodha Chandrodaya Nataka mentions Purushottama shrine, and Anantavarman Chodaganga began the Jagannath Temple; shortened to Puri from Purushottama Puri)
b_puri.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit/Odia Puri ('the city'), shortened from Purushottama Puri ('city of Purushottama / Jagannath').

b_ganjam.first_mention_attestation: Early modern town/district name (Potagarh fort built 1768 CE) with no datable pre-867 CE attestation of the form Ganjam
b_ganjam.etymology_analysis: Odia Ganjam, derived either from Persian ganj ('granary, market') or as a later evolution of the 7th-century CE regional name Kongoda.

historical_names.name: Kongoda
historical_names.source: Ganjam copper-plate grant of Shailodbhava ruler Madhavaraja II (620 CE)
historical_names.notes: The Ganjam region was known as Kongoda (Kangoda) under the Shailodbhava dynasty in the 7th century CE, attested in the 620 CE Ganjam grant.

b_gopalpur.first_mention_attestation: Modern coastal town name (Gopalpur-on-Sea) in Ganjam district, Odisha, with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation
b_gopalpur.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit/Odia Gopalpur ('town of Gopal/Krishna'), a historic coastal port in Ganjam district, Odisha.

b_rayapura.first_mention_attestation: c. 1400 CE (Raipur stone inscription of Kalachuri ruler Brahmadeva of the Raipur branch, late 14th to early 15th century CE)

eponym.details: Traditionally named after Brahmdeo Rai (Brahmadeva), the late 14th- to early 15th-century CE Kalachuri ruler of the Raipur branch (son of Ramachandra).

b_rayapura.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit/Chhattisgarhi Rayapura ('city of Rai', modern Raipur), capital of the Raipur Kalachuri branch established in the late 14th to early 15th century CE.

b_shivapura.first_mention_attestation: Generic Sanskritized settlement name in Dakshina Kosala / Chhattisgarh with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation
b_shivapura.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Shivapura ('city of Shiva'), a generic temple-town designation in the Dakshina Kosala region.

b_camparanya.first_mention_attestation: 1479 CE (birthplace of Vaishnava saint Vallabhacharya; formerly known as Champajhar)
b_camparanya.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Champaranya ('forest of champa flowers'), modern Champaran in Raipur district, Chhattisgarh, famed as the 1479 CE birthplace of Vallabhacharya.
